facts.statement: Mongolosaurus was a titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Mongolosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur which lived during the Early Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore named and described the species Mongolosaurus haplodon in 1933.
facts.quote: In 1933 Charles W. Gilmore, based on this fossil, named and described the type species Mongolosaurus haplodon.

facts.statement: The genus name Mongolosaurus refers to Mongolia.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 6710 was found in the Early Cretaceous On Gong Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, AMNH 6710, was found in the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian) On Gong Formation.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses recovered Mongolosaurus as a derived member of the clade Lognkosauria, sister to Jiangxititan.
facts.quote: They recovered Mongolosaurus as a derived member of the titanosaurian clade Lognkosauria, as the sister taxon to Jiangxititan.

facts.statement: Mongolosaurus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Mongolosaurus belongs to the parent group Titanosauria.
